subject: research/capture-storage
professional: a senior digital imaging technician (DIT) / media-workflow engineer who designs on-set and travel offload kits (multi-destination checksum-verified copies with Hedge, ShotPut Pro or Silverstack, 3-2-1 backup practice), reading it as a systems-modelling researcher would; first checks: can one card be read by more than one reader, is a second backup copy a second read of the card or a multi-destination write, and does the evening-time headline survive the per-card read time

evidence.correctness: The arithmetic reproduces but the offload model, which carries the headline, is physically wrong. Independent recompute (/tmp/claude-0/audit-cs/recompute.py, run with /usr/bin/python3.13 -I, no subject import): GB/h 54/45/27/90 at 120/100/60/200 Mbit/s (decimal), 4-camera day 864 GB, 6.048 TB a week, one reader one copy 2.667 h, battery/card ratios 609/658/975/439, sourced day 900 GB: all match results.txt and README. But model.py:62 treats N readers as N x 90 MB/s of divisible bandwidth over the whole day's bytes, so the optimiser picks more readers than there are cards in every feasible row of results.txt table B (1 card/2 readers, 2/3, 3/4, 5/6, 6/7, 7/8). A card can be read by only one reader at a time. Re-modelled with per-card serial reads and an LPT schedule (/tmp/claude-0/audit-cs/makespan.py): under the subject's own two-pass copy assumption no rig of 1 to 8 cameras meets the 1 h limit (a single 216 GB card read twice at 90 MB/s takes 1.33 h), so the headline '6 readers, 4 SSDs, 452 g' and the 1-camera '160 g, 2 readers, 0.67 h' are infeasible plans. With per-card reads and a single-read multi-destination copy, the 4-camera plan is 3 readers, 377 g, 1.00 h. The qualitative conclusion (time, not card weight, binds) survives and is if anything stronger.

Defects: sourced.use() swaps module globals by setattr (not re-entrant or thread-safe; a function-argument parameter set would be cleaner); PARAMS rows ssd_g, reader_g, reader_mbs_model are documentary only, sourced_set() never reads them, so editing them changes nothing, while the README tells a person to 'fill PARAMS'; per_cam is recomputed inside the 72-iteration loop though it depends only on the card size; `from .model import *` package API; no input validation (unknown camera name is a KeyError, hours<=0 is accepted).

But the headline 'a safe plan needs 6 parallel readers and 4 SSDs, about 450 g' (README:3, research/README.md:735, project.json summary) is backed by a file only in the sense that results.txt prints it: the plan is not physically realisable (see correctness). evidence.fitness: A researcher can rerun everything in seconds, but there is little to build on: it is a back-of-envelope sizing calculation (bitrate x hours, divide by a throughput) with one optimiser whose core time model is wrong. Nearest prior work is DIT practice and tooling, none cited: multi-destination checksum-verified offload (Hedge, ShotPut Pro, Pomfort Silverstack, which read a card once and write N copies), the 3-2-1 backup rule, and camera-vendor offload guidance. The result (copy time, not card mass, binds; verify while copying) is what that practice already assumes. Nothing here is new or near the PhD/publishable bar in research/CLAUDE.md; it reads as one micro-question, not a programme step.
evidence.domain: A DIT would reject the offload method on two points. (a) Parallelism: throughput is bounded per card (one card, one reader), so the evening is a makespan over card loads, and the largest card (the mirrorless body's 360 GB day on a 512 GB card, 1.11 h at 90 MB/s even read once) sets a floor no reader count removes; the model ignores it. (b) Copies: standard practice reads the card once and writes both SSD copies simultaneously (multi-destination), so the second copy costs SSD write bandwidth, not a second card read; the model doubles the card-read time (model.py:64). It also ignores the shared USB/host bus that 6 to 8 readers saturate (stated as a limit). The checksum section is sound and matches practice (hash inline while copying).

defects.what: Offload time treats readers as divisible bandwidth over the whole day (day / (readers x 90 MB/s)); a card can be read by only one reader, so every feasible plan in results.txt uses more readers than cards (1 card/2 readers for one camera) and, under the model's own two-pass copy, no rig of 1-8 cameras actually fits the 1 h limit. The headline '6 readers, 4 SSDs, 452 g' (README:3, research/README.md:735, project.json) is not a realisable plan. Repro: PYTHONPATH=src python3 -c "from capture_storage import offload; print(offload(['360 camera'],4,7))" -> readers=2, cards=1, offload_h=0.667; expected infeasible (one 216 GB card read twice at 90 MB/s = 1.33 h).

Second backup copy is modelled as a second full read of the cards (t *= copies), against standard multi-destination offload practice (read once, write N copies, checksum inline). It roughly doubles reader count and inflates the headline grams (6 readers/452 g vs 3 readers/377 g for the 4-camera rig with per-card reads); the README does not state the assumption.
Tests pin no plan and never check readers <= cards: 4 of 5 seeded mutants in core logic survive (copies factor dropped, reader grams once, SSD headroom removed, battery g/h halved).

No prior work cited and no novelty: digital-imaging-technician offload practice (Hedge, ShotPut Pro, Silverstack multi-destination verified copies, 3-2-1 rule) already settles 'time binds, verify while copying'; the project is a single sizing calculation, far from the research/CLAUDE.md programme bar.
're-reading the cards too doubles the evening to 4.8 h' drops the 0.62 h SSD re-read the sentence has just added; with both re-reads the evening is 5.4 h.

PARAMS rows ssd_g, reader_g and reader_mbs_model are never read by sourced_set(), so the README's advice to 'fill PARAMS in minutes' changes no result for those figures; use() monkeypatches module globals instead of passing parameters.

verdict: A tidy, fully reproducible sizing note (15 tests pass, results.txt and the figure regenerate byte-identically, every README number traces to a results file, data rates and battery/card ratios recompute exactly), whose central optimiser is physically wrong: it splits one evening's bytes over up to 8 readers as if bandwidth were divisible, so every reported plan uses more readers than there are cards, and once a card is read by one reader at a time no rig meets the 1 h limit under the project's own two-pass copy assumption. The headline '6 readers, 452 g' is therefore not a realisable kit; the qualitative finding (copy time, not card mass, binds) survives and is stronger than stated. Verification is weak (4 of 5 seeded bugs survive), the second-copy model departs from standard multi-destination offload practice, and no DIT prior work is cited. Finished as described, but well below the research bar.
